title: observability: token-level metrics, tracing, logging, dashboards and alert tuning
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Adds token-level cost/latency dashboards, enhanced tracing spans for inference and KV cache, structured logging for cache events, and tuned alerts to reduce noise while preserving SLO coverage.
description: Motivation: Recent incidents and ongoing noise from high-rate alerts revealed we lacked token-level visibility across the serving stack. This PR adds token-level metrics, improves tracing spans and structured logging for KV cache events, ships a Grafana dashboard with cost/latency breakdowns by token position and model variant, and tunes alert thresholds and burn-rate rules to reduce false positives. Scope: 1) metrics: per-token latency and cost aggregation, cache-hit-rate by token prefix, and model-variant dimensioning; 2) tracing: add token_id and token_index to key spans (request, decode, kv-lookup), include sampling hints for high-latency tokens; 3) logging: structured KV cache logs (event_type, key_hash, hit, ttl_ms) that feed into our log-based metrics; 4) dashboards: Grafana dashboard JSON + dashboard provisioning; 5) alerts: burn-rate based alert rules and per-route thresholds to reduce noisy alerts during traffic spikes. Checklist: - [x] metrics instrumentation (prometheus counters/histograms) - [x] tracing additions + schema bump - [x] structured logging + log-to-metrics mapping - [x] Grafana dashboard (token-level cost/latency) - [x] alert rules updated and tested in staging - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] docs updated (observability/README) Backwards compatibility: metrics/tracing additions are additive and behind a feature flag (observability.token_level.enabled=false by default). Documentation: included dashboard README and migration notes for log-based metrics ingestion. Monitoring impact: Initial alert thresholds tuned conservatively; we expect a ~40% reduction in noisy alerts based on staging traffic replay. Follow-ups: (ENG-3391) add sampling for token-level traces at 1% default and 100% for errors, (ENG-3405) add ML-based anomaly detector for token-cost regressions.

review_comments: Evan Jacobs (reviewer): Nice end-to-end PR. A few things: 1) can we avoid high-cardinality labels for token text; token_index and token_bucket are fine. 2) Ensure Prometheus cardinality docs are updated. 3) Can we simulate bursty traffic in staging to validate burn-rate behavior?
Priya Nair (author): Thanks Evan — yes we avoided token text and added token_bucket (0-15). Updated docs in observability/README.md. Replayed 48-hour traffic in staging (see test outputs).
Carlos Mendez (reviewer): Tracing: please add schema version bump and document new fields in tracing.md. Also add a warning about sampling cost in token-level traces.
Priya Nair (author): bump added (tracing_schema: v2) and notes added to docs. We gated tracing field emission behind observability.token_level.tracing=true and default to false.

Asha Patel (reviewer): Alert tuning looks reasonable. Two suggestions: 1) add a recovery window to the burn-rate alert, 2) adjust severity for non-prod routes. I left inline comments on token_level_alerts.yaml.

Priya Nair (author): Applied both suggestions. Recovery window set to 30m and severity lowered for routes matching /sandbox/* in the alert rule. CI: integration test for alerts had a timeout which I increased.
Evan Jacobs (approver): Approved after changes. Verified staging dashboards and alert firing behavior against replay.
ci_checks: ci/integration_tests: fail (dashboard provisioning timeout) -> rerun -> pass
summary: Implements token-level observability: metrics, tracing, structured logging, dashboard and alert tuning. Reduces alert noise while providing fine-grained cost/latency breakdowns by token position and model variant.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag: observability.token_level.enabled=false by default. To enable in staging: set observability.token_level.enabled=true and observability.token_level.tracing=true for targeted services. Dashboard provisioning handled by deploy/grafana/provisioning. Alert recalibration recommended after 24-48h of production traffic and a separate run of the burn-rate replay tool.
risk_assessment: Low: all changes behind feature flags; metrics/tracing additions are additive. Main risk is Prometheus cardinality if operator enables token-level labels without token_bucket aggregation. Mitigation: default disable and docs + alerting to detect cardinality spikes.
